entries.originalText: It is Truth which we must look for in Holy Writ, not cunning of words.
entries.modernizedText: It is Truth we must look for in Holy Scripture, not cleverness of words.

entries.originalText: All Scripture ought to be read in the spirit in which it was written.
entries.modernizedText: All Scripture ought to be read in the spirit in which it was written.

entries.originalText: We must rather seek for what is profitable in Scripture, than for what ministereth to subtlety in discourse.
entries.modernizedText: We must seek what is profitable in Scripture rather than what serves subtlety in discussion.

entries.originalText: Therefore we ought to read books which are devotional and simple, as well as those which are deep and difficult.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, we ought to read devotional and simple books as well as those that are deep and difficult.

entries.originalText: And let not the weight of the writer be a stumbling-block to thee, whether he be of little or much learning, but let the love of the pure Truth draw thee to read.
entries.modernizedText: And do not let the standing of the writer be a stumbling block to you, whether he has little or much learning, but let love of the pure Truth draw you to read.

entries.originalText: Ask not, who hath said this or that, but look to what he says.
entries.modernizedText: Do not ask who has said this or that, but look to what he says.

entries.originalText: Men pass away, but the truth of the Lord endureth for ever.
entries.modernizedText: People pass away, but the truth of the Lord endures forever.

entries.originalText: Without respect of persons God speaketh to us in divers manners.
entries.modernizedText: Without respect of persons, God speaks to us in various ways.

entries.originalText: Our own curiosity often hindereth us in the reading of holy writings, when we seek to understand and discuss, where we should pass simply on.
entries.modernizedText: Our own curiosity often hinders us in reading holy writings, when we seek to understand and discuss where we should simply pass on.

entries.originalText: If thou wouldst profit by thy reading, read humbly, simply, honestly, and not desiring to win a character for learning.
entries.modernizedText: If you want to benefit from your reading, read humbly, simply, and honestly, without desiring to gain a reputation for learning.

entries.originalText: Ask freely, and hear in silence the words of holy men; nor be displeased at the hard sayings of older men than thou, for they are not uttered without cause.
entries.modernizedText: Ask freely, and listen in silence to the words of holy men; do not be displeased at the hard sayings of those older than you, for they are not spoken without cause.
